# Question 1 (20 points)

William Sealy Gosset worked at Guinness, where he needed to draw reliable conclusions from small, costly brewing experiments. He developed the t distribution to account for the extra uncertainty that arises when the population standard deviation is estimated from a small sample. He published under the name “Student,” giving Student’s t test its name.

Dataset: beer.csv. One randomly selected bottle from each of 100 independent batches. batch identifies the batch; abv is alcohol by volume, expressed as a percentage (4.2 means 4.2% ABV). Assume the population is approximately normal; its standard deviation is unknown.

Does the population mean alcohol content differ from the target of 4.2%? Complete the analysis described in the instructions. Explain whether a statistically significant difference must matter to customers.


a. Summarize the data (i.e., visual and quantitative EDA).
b. Use plots to check assumptions.
c. State the null and alternative hypotheses. 
d. Run the appropriate test. Report the test statistic, p-value, and confidence interval.
e. Interpret the results. 


**Answer:**


# Question 2 (20 points)

**Dataset: `reminders.csv`.** Forty-eight defendants were randomly assigned to Standard or Enhanced appointment reminders. Each attended one appointment. `defendant_id` identifies the person, `group` records the reminder, and `minutes_early` measures arrival time. Negative values mean late arrival.

Do the population mean arrival times differ? Define the difference as Enhanced minus Standard.

a. Summarize the data (i.e., visual and quantitative EDA).
b. Use plots to check assumptions.
c. State the null and alternative hypotheses. 
d. Run the appropriate test. Report the test statistic, p-value, and confidence interval.
e. Interpret the results.

# Question 3 (20 points)

**Dataset: `filing.csv`.** Fifteen randomly sampled court clerks each processed equivalent packets before and after electronic filing was introduced. `clerk_id` identifies the clerk; `before` and `after` are completion times in minutes. Different clerks are independent. Everyone completed the before assessment first; there was no comparison group.

Did the population mean completion time change? Complete the analysis described in the instructions, defining the difference as before minus after.

Which values need to be approximately normal for this test? Explain one reason the observed change might not be caused by electronic filing.
